speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) what did TUV Rheinland's report on the hairline cracks found on defective MRT trains reveal; and (b) whether the Ministry will make the entire report public in the interest of transparency.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Did the report also make similar recommendation that you all should replace the body as well?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Or is it just Kawasaki's decision to replace it on goodwill?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Relying on memory, I do not think the report talked about car-body.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I can understand, as an engineer, why they decided to take this course of action.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is a little bit like when you extensively 	Page: 25 renovate your house.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Sometimes, the contractor will tell you, I think, in all honesty, it is better you tear it down and rebuild.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If it is massive renovation, they find that it is more troublesome and, perhaps, it may even take longer and, sometimes, they do recommend to simply tear it down and rebuild.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Let us understand a little bit of the process here.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The bolster is welded, as I said, to the car-body and then the car-body carries all the engines, the seats, glass windows, and so on.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The bolster is the one that has some problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If you were to reuse the car-body, then what it means is that, first, you got to cut out the bolster from the car-body.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And then when you receive the new bolster, you got to find a way to weld it to the car-body.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Of course, they do not speak Singlish, but they probably said, "Aiyah, so 'leceh'.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Let's just produce a new car-body and get a new piece of bolster and weld it on."
